stamp.cpu_clock: CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID of the report thread; the measurement runs on a current-thread tokio runtime, so every decode the production fetcher does lands on that thread

decision_rule: Per subject: GO when rare/bytes_ratio_100gb <= 0.1 and sidecar/over_postings <= 1.2 and build/cpu_ratio <= 1.5 and delete/rebuild_cpu_over_compaction reported and delete/bytes_over_object reported and delete/residual_terms <= 0, each reported exactly once. Overall: GO when every pre-registered subject of the arm is GO.

blocks.unpredicted: fixed by construction: objects * object_rows / block_records

objects.unpredicted: fixed by construction: max_lines / object_rows whole objects

decision.line: fulltext_sidecar decision hdfs_sidecar: NO-GO (rare/bytes_ratio_100gb=0.0978<=0.1 ok, sidecar/over_postings=4.3145<=1.2 FAIL, build/cpu_ratio=1.1800<=1.5 ok, delete/rebuild_cpu_over_compaction=1.4951 ok, delete/bytes_over_object=0.5287 ok, delete/residual_terms=0.0000<=0 ok)

notes: objects: 10 of 524288 rows from the first 5242880 corpus lines, written by the production RlogWriter (bloom over every field); keys t13/sidecar/0000.rlog..t13/sidecar/0009.rlog

sidecar: row-granular inverted index of the production body tokens, term blocks of sidecar_stride prefix-shared terms with delta-coded row ordinals, each zstd-compressed, then a zstd index (first term, offset, length per block; rows per RLOG block) and an 8-byte trailer. A real build and a real probe through ranged GETs, not a simulation

baselines: the BLOOM section the production writer wrote, its verdict through the production scan funnel scan_accounted_with_tenant with HasWord(body) over the object's full time window, every returned row checked against the corpus. rare/default_path_* is that scan with the production defaults: every block is a time candidate, the 0.75 coverage crossover fires before the bloom is consulted, and the whole object is read. rare/no_crossover_* is the same scan with the crossover off (BlockRangeFetcher coverage threshold 2.0): the ranged read still fetches every time candidate block, because production narrows by BLOOM only at decode over the fetched buffer. rare/bloom_* is the bloom-guided route production does not take, the baseline the decision is taken against: real ranged GETs of the production suffix probe (DEFAULT_LOG_SUFFIX_LEN), PAGE_DIR and BLOOM where the probe missed them, and the pages of the blocks the production bloom kept, each round coalesced at DEFAULT_LOG_REQUEST_COST_BYTES; its block verdict is the production scan's. rare/plan_route_bytes_per_object is what the production plan_segment for the same query moves per object before any scan (the first sampled token, once per object); the POSTINGS section the production encode_postings_section builds over body tokens to block indices (uncapped, so its size is what it would cost; postings/capped_objects counts the objects where the production distinct cap would have dropped it)

costs: GETs and the bytes they returned, counted by the production InstrumentedStore, through a fresh LogSegmentFetcher per object and token (no cache); every returned row on both paths equals the corpus rows holding the token

100 GB: scale_objects = scale_raw_bytes / (raw_bytes / objects) = 100000000000 / (729267580 / 10); per token cost = sum(measured costs of its matching objects) + (scale_objects - matching objects) * mean miss cost; mean miss bytes bloom 1162157.9, sidecar 107654.9, default path 8097652.9; mean miss GETs bloom 3.041, sidecar 2.000; ratio = mean sidecar cost / mean bloom cost over 30 tokens

build: build/sidecar_cpu_ms is the thread CPU of tokenizing the decoded bodies and encoding the sidecar; build/compaction_cpu_ms is the thread CPU of decoding every block and re-encoding with the production writer; rewrite amplification is (objects + sidecars) / objects in bytes written

deletion: erased row 13 of object 0 (1 terms only it held); the object is rewritten without it by the production writer and the sidecar rebuilt from the rewritten rows (a sidecar cannot be edited in place: every later ordinal moves); each erased-only term was probed in the rebuilt sidecar, and the row after the erased one was found at its new place; rebuild CPU is over object 0's compaction CPU
